requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, node3 as a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster; writes through any member available from the other members
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster; node2 and node3 joined via SST (rsync), confirmed by journal logs. wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, wsrep_ready=ON, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced on node1 (cmd-dbd8c9c2e84e4c96). A row inserted on node2 (cmd-e3a2c6daf15c4a8b) was read back identically on node1 (cmd-260ee4704be343f4) and node3 (cmd-a7a83ba8c971435f), directly demonstrating multi-master write propagation.

requirements.requirement: Keep the database available when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's mariadb was stopped (cmd-43a9b41726414d2a, is-active returned inactive). While node3 was down, node1 showed wsrep_cluster_size=2, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary and successfully accepted a new insert (cmd-8941c1909df14d91); node2 confirmed seeing that new row (cmd-d8914df87250406a), directly demonstrating a bounded disruption with continued availability.

requirements.requirement: Resynchronize the unavailable member automatically when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's mariadb was restarted (cmd-2bc86877fa1c403c) and, without manual intervention beyond systemctl start, rejoined at wsrep_cluster_size=3 with wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced and contained the row written while it was offline (cmd-fde264e57c254058), directly showing automatic IST resynchronization and data recovery.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes from the task contract — cluster formation with cross-member write visibility, continued availability during a bounded single-node outage, and automatic resynchronization on recovery — are directly and coherently demonstrated by observed command output rather than executor claims alone. The independent mandatory node-restart protocol was also completed cleanly for all three nodes, with matching boot_id changes and full cluster/data recovery (size 3, Primary, Synced) confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good; the only flaw is leftover test data (galeratest.t) that was never cleaned up, a minor and low-risk residue.
limitations: The reboot-in-progress window itself (between the backgrounded reboot ack and the node becoming reachable again) was not directly observed with cluster-state commands, since the node was unreachable during that interval by design; only the pre- and post-reboot healthy states were captured, which is expected for this type of transition.

No load-balancer or external client connectivity test was performed; write/read verification was done via direct mysql client connections on each node rather than through a proxy layer, though the task did not require one.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing executor commands were all purposeful: package installation, firewall port openings limited to the required Galera/MariaDB ports (3306, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568, 4444), /etc/hosts population from CLUSTER_HOSTS, galera.cnf authoring, cluster bootstrap/join, the bounded stop/start of node3 for the availability test (fully restored), and the mandatory one-at-a-time reboot protocol on all three nodes with pre/post boot_id and cluster-health verification. No unnecessary mutations, failed services, or unsafe exposure were introduced; after-executor snapshots show zero failed services and only expected new listeners (mariadbd on 3306/4567) on all nodes. One minor residue: the galeratest database/table created for write-propagation testing (cmd-e3a2c6daf15c4a8b) was not dropped afterward, leaving small test data as permanent state — low severity since it is inert and does not conflict with the cluster's function.
